original_paper_or_source: Aguilar et al. (2020) — LinCE: A Centralized Benchmark for Linguistic Code-switching Evaluation
languages_covered: Spanish-English; Hindi-English; Modern Standard Arabic-Egyptian Arabic; Nepali-English
dataset_size_description: ~16,000 tokens across 4 tasks (NER, POS, LID, Sentiment)
task_type: NER; POS tagging; Language ID; Sentiment Analysis
relevance_to_this_study: HIGH — LinCE includes Hindi-English code-mixed data directly relevant to the Hinglish evaluation condition in this study. The Language Identification sub-task aligns with our Code-Mix Detector validation methodology.
decision: APPROVED FOR REFERENCE — not for data ingestion
decision_rationale: The LinCE benchmark provides an established evaluation framework for code-mixed Hindi-English NLP. While the task types (NER/POS/LID/Sentiment) differ from our faithfulness evaluation, it validates that Hinglish (Roman-script Hindi-English) is a legitimate and studied linguistic phenomenon. We cite LinCE for motivation and methodology grounding rather than directly ingesting its data into our RAG corpus.
integration_plan: Cite in literature review and CODE_MIXED_DATA_GUIDELINES.md. Do not ingest into the RAG knowledge base.

original_paper_or_source: Khanuja et al. (2020) — GLUECoS: An Evaluation Benchmark for Code-Switched NLP
dataset_size_description: ~8,000 examples across 6 NLU tasks (Language ID, NER, POS, QA, Sentiment, NLI)
task_type: Question Answering; Sentiment Analysis; NLI; Language ID; NER; POS
relevance_to_this_study: HIGH — GLUECoS Hindi-English QA task directly parallels our study design: code-mixed Hinglish queries matched against English knowledge sources. The QA task establishes precedent for evaluating retrieval performance in cross-lingual settings.
decision: APPROVED FOR REFERENCE — not for data ingestion
decision_rationale: GLUECoS validates our experimental design at a methodological level. The Hindi-English QA split shows that LLMs can be evaluated on code-mixed queries targeting English knowledge, supporting our baseline vs. mitigation paradigm. The MIT license permits citation and derivative research. We do not ingest GLUECoS data into our corpus because our corpus is domain-specific (banking/telecom) and our queries are hand-crafted to match corpus documents.
integration_plan: Cite in study protocol and literature review. Discuss QA task as analogous setup in FINAL_STUDY_PROTOCOL.md.

original_paper_or_source: Artetxe et al. (2020) — On the Cross-lingual Transferability of Monolingual Representations
languages_covered: English; Spanish; German; Greek; Russian; Turkish; Arabic; Vietnamese; Thai; Chinese; Hindi (11 languages)
relevance_to_this_study: MEDIUM — XQuAD demonstrates cross-lingual retrieval and QA at scale and includes Hindi as a target language. However, XQuAD uses script-native Hindi (Devanagari) rather than Romanized Hinglish, and its domains (Wikipedia general knowledge) do not match our banking/telecom corpus.
decision_rationale: XQuAD establishes strong precedent for cross-lingual QA research and validates multilingual evaluation methodology. However, the Romanized code-mixed Hinglish in our study (e.g., 'bank mein UPI ka daily limit kitna hai?') is a different phenomenon from script-native cross-lingual transfer. We cite XQuAD as background to position our study within the broader cross-lingual NLP literature.
integration_plan: Background citation only. Do not directly compare our Recall@K scores to XQuAD benchmarks.

original_paper_or_source: Lewis et al. (2020) — MLQA: Evaluating Cross-lingual Extractive Question Answering
languages_covered: English; Arabic; German; Spanish; Hindi; Vietnamese; Chinese (7 languages)
dataset_size_description: ~5,000 QA instances per language aligned across languages
relevance_to_this_study: MEDIUM — MLQA includes Hindi and establishes cross-lingual QA evaluation precedent. Same limitation as XQuAD: uses script-native Hindi, not Romanized Hinglish code-mixing.
decision_rationale: Complements XQuAD as background cross-lingual QA benchmark. Demonstrates the gap our study fills: existing multilingual benchmarks use clean, script-native translations, whereas real-world South Asian users produce intra-sentential Romanized code-mixed queries. Our study is novel in evaluating RAG faithfulness under this authentic user behavior.

original_paper_or_source: Kakwani et al. (2020) — IndicNLPSuite: Monolingual Corpora, Evaluation Benchmarks and Pre-trained Multilingual Language Models for Indian Languages
languages_covered: Hindi; Bengali; Marathi; Gujarati; Telugu; Tamil; Kannada; Malayalam; Punjabi; Oriya; Assamese (11 Indic languages)
task_type: Article Classification; Named Entity Recognition; Headline Prediction; Sentiment Analysis; Extractive QA
relevance_to_this_study: MEDIUM — IndicGLUE covers Tamil and Hindi at the script-native level (not Romanized code-mixed). Provides strong precedent for NLP evaluation on Indian languages. The corpus does not include Romanized transliteration.
decision_rationale: IndicGLUE establishes the Indian NLP evaluation landscape, supporting the motivation for our study. Tamil and Hindi are covered, but exclusively in their native scripts (Tamil script; Devanagari). Our study uniquely targets the Romanized code-mixed register, filling a gap that IndicGLUE does not address.
integration_plan: Background citation. Note distinction between script-native Indian language NLP and Romanized code-mixing.

benchmark_name: XTREME (Cross-lingual Transfer Evaluation of Multilingual Encoders)
original_paper_or_source: Hu et al. (2020) — XTREME: A Massively Multilingual Multi-task Benchmark for Evaluating Cross-lingual Generalization
domains: Wikipedia; Universal Dependencies; Wikidata; XNLI; SQuAD
dataset_size_description: 9 tasks including QA, NER, POS, dependency parsing, sentence retrieval
relevance_to_this_study: LOW-MEDIUM — XTREME is the state-of-the-art multilingual generalization benchmark. However, it does not include code-mixed data; all languages are evaluated in their native scripts. Relevant for positioning the embedding model (multilingual-e5-base) within the multilingual NLP space.
decision_rationale: XTREME validates the use of multilingual encoder models (like multilingual-e5-base) for cross-lingual retrieval tasks. Positions our embedding choice within established multilingual NLP practice.
integration_plan: Background citation for embedding model justification only.
